liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (3 reviews): Reviewer was struck that Viola Lee Blues appears in this show; Reviewer ranks this among favorite Viola Lees: funky driving groove, Jerry riffing between lines, Phil walking scales on bass [8][12][16]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer says first three songs are rough, but The Other One may be the best ever; Reviewer says Cryptical into The Other One sounds like a fusion band, with stretched tempos and telepathic improvisation [14][18]
- **Alligator** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the first-set Alligator smoking; Alligator contains a false start [2][18]
- **Foxy Lady Jam** (1 review): Reviewer was struck that a Foxy Lady jam appears in this show [8]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer counts this Dark Star among favorite versions of all time [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Foxy Lady Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]
- **Clementine**: rare: 7 archived performances [19]
- **Born Cross Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.clugston.6182.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 177 min; rated 3.67/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quality incredible on this soundboard source [7]
- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.miller.88465.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 153 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Transfer was cleaned up with levels fixed; the tape runs out during Feedback [2]
- **gd69-04-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.19841.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 147 min; rated 4.37/5 by 35 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound superb and band tight, but the end of Feedback is cut short; Reviewer finds sound quite good, with slight hiss that the performance outweighs; Reviewer praises the mix as perfect, with Phil's bass very prominent [9][11][16]
- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.ashley.89717.vobf**: soundboard; 0 songs; 0 min [6]. Said about its sound: Main source restored nearly pristine; patches, from multiple analog generations, could not be restored as well [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the Winterland show of 10/25/69 is even better than this one [10]
- Reviewer disagrees this is the greatest Eleven, pointing instead to the 10/12/68 version [14]
- Reviewer prefers this night over the other two nights of the run [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.clugston.6182.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Possible generation updated to MSR to DAT to CDR; earlier marked MSR to cassette to DAT to CDR; Intro comes from an alternate soundboard; some tracks have reel cuts; 1/20/68 material used as filler; via Scott Clugston and Lee Revell [1]
- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.miller.88465.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD D [2]
- **gd69-04-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.19841.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller and J. Ashley; source: Soundboard - Bertha Remaster [5]. Also: Reviewer guesses the taper reached the end of the reel, causing the Feedback cutoff [9]
- **gd1969-04-21.sbd.ashley.89717.vobf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: Bertha Remaster of the patched Master Reel source 88465. [6]. Also: Remastered with the Bertha DAW, completed January 28, 2007; main source and patches processed separately [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead The Ark, Boston Poster Apr. '69](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/ark-boston-poster-apr-69) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead The Ark - April 21, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/april-21-1969) [21]
